title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 654–656). Grothendieck is preparing the construction of pro-group schemes over a base S attached to extensions of discrete groups, and the projective system of finite-index sublattices of a lattice M.

Setup from the previous page:
- S is noetherian and quasi-compact; n ≥ 1.
- S_0 = V(n) is the closed subscheme where n = 0, and U = S \ S_0 = S[1/n] is assumed schematically dense in S.
- G is an affine S-group scheme.
- φ_U : G_{a,U} → G_U is a homomorphism of group schemes.
- Proposition: there is a power m = n^r such that φ_U ∘ u_m (where u_m(λ) = mλ) extends to a homomorphism ψ_m : G_{a,S} → G.

This page proves the proposition.
1. Reduction to schemes. By schematic density of U (hence of G_{a,U} in G_{a,S}, and of G_{a,U} ×_U G_{a,U} in G_{a,S} ×_S G_{a,S}), extensions are unique. Any extension that is merely a morphism of schemes is then automatically a group homomorphism.
2. Reduction to affine S. One may assume S = Spec A. Let B be the ring of G. Then U = Spec A_n with A_n = A[1/n], and G_U has ring B_n = B ⊗_A A_n. The comorphism of φ_U is (23) B_n → A_n[T].
3. The twist. The comorphism of φ_U ∘ u_m is the composite of (23) with (24) A_n[T] → A_n[T], T ↦ mT.
4. The key computation. For x = Σ_{i≤N} a_i T^i with a_i ∈ A_n:
   - u_m^*(x) = Σ a_i m^i T^i.
   - Since there are finitely many a_i, each with an n-power denominator, for m = n^ν with ν large we get m^i a_i ∈ A for all i ≥ 1.
   - Hence u_m^*(x) ≡ a_0 mod A[T], so (25): u_m^*(x) ∈ A[T] for large ν ⇔ a_0 ∈ A.
5. Conclusion (next page). Apply this to the images of finitely many A-algebra generators of B; this needs G of finite type. Note that a_0 = x(0) is the pullback along the zero section.
   - Corollary: for a morphism of schemes u : A^1_U → G_U, some n-power twist u(m·) extends over S iff the section u(0) of G_U extends to a section of G over S.
   - For a group homomorphism, u(0) is the unit section, which is defined over S. So the condition is automatic and the proposition follows.
   - A Remark ties this to a 'théorème' p. 662' for noetherian S of dimension 1 with generic point of characteristic 0, i.e. the arithmetic case such as Spec Z or Spec of a ring of integers.

In short, the page shows that denominators in n of a G_a-homomorphism, or of an affine line, over S[1/n] are killed by rescaling the parameter by a large power of n.
errors: The proposition as stated on the previous page only assumes G affine; the argument needs B finitely generated over A (G of finite type). The next page's corollary adds 'de t.f.'.
Noetherianity is not really used. What is needed is that A → A[1/n] is injective (schematic density of U) and that S is quasi-compact, so that one ν works on a finite affine cover.
Notational slips: '(25) ψ_m(x)' should be ψ_m^*(x), and ψ_m^* is really u_m^*. Also 'φ_u se prolonge' should read 'φ_U ∘ u_m se prolonge'.

ideas.what: Extension of a morphism A^1_{S[1/n]} → G after rescaling T ↦ n^ν T: denominators disappear except in the constant term. Hence an extension exists iff the image of the origin extends.
ideas.modern_name: Clearing denominators by rescaling / integral models of homomorphisms G_a → G (spreading out)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (elementary commutative algebra); similar arguments occur in integral exponential/Lazard-type contexts
ideas.where_published: not as such; a standard EGA IV-style limit/density argument

ideas.what: Uniqueness of extensions and the automatic group-homomorphism property via schematic density of U = S[1/n]

deep.surprise_reason: A correct but elementary lemma: clearing n-power denominators by rescaling T, in service of the Longue Marche construction of pro-group schemes attached to discrete groups/lattices. The broader programme it serves is of some historical interest, but this page itself contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: 'OPS $\mathcal{S}$ [affine], A son anneau' is presumably 'On peut supposer S affine, A son anneau'.
'Donc l'anneau de $\mathcal{A}$ sur[?]' should be 'Donc l'anneau de U sera A_n = A[1/n]'.
'$\psi_{mu}$' should be ψ_{m,U}, or φ_U ∘ u_m; '(24) $\psi_m^*$' is u_m^*.
The struck line reads approximately 'ψ_m^*(x) = Σ m^i a_i T^i ∈ A[T]', not '$\ni m^iT^i \in A$'.
